metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly; reduce forecast slope after peak and introduce mean-reversion decay factor.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility bias; dampen forecast variance and anchor to recent 7-day moving average.
- In low-sentiment periods, model often fails to recognize downward trend continuation; enforce downward drift correction if 3 consecutive days show price decline.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently misreads long-term trend; use 18-day weighted average as baseline and adjust for 3–5% downward drift if recent 5-day average is below 30-day average.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after spike, model often fails to anticipate; add lagged correction: if true price drops >5% from peak, reduce forecast by 2–3% for next 3 days.
